agent_note: First-person narrator. Every narration beat embedded in the dialogue quotes is past tense ('My hammer collided', 'The gargoyle led me down the nave', 'six silk robes waited', 'I whispered', 'Rory's eyes flitted', 'was trained on Four'), which is the strongest available evidence and points retrospective. Quotation marks survive on most multi-speaker quotes, so mark-majority was the primary dialogue signal; for the unmarked ones (q10060, q10061, q10062, q10072, q10078) the signal was vocative/direct address and register. Page is heavily aphoristic: 7 gnomic of 26. Only 4 event quotes (2 past / 2 present) -- thin, and both present ones are reflective first-person states rather than moment-by-moment action, so they are the softest calls here. q10061 is worth a second look: read as speech to the gargoyle it is dialogue, but read as the novel's oral frame it would be event/present and would shift the narrating situation toward dual.
